transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been having these mornings where I wake up and think… it might have been easier if I just hadn’t woken up at all. That scared me. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but the thoughts are there, and I felt like I needed to tell someone.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Yes… I think I have. Not constantly, but more than usual. Some days I just feel low and kind of weighed down, even when nothing specific has happened.
Have you been feeling this low for at least two weeks?
Yes. It’s been about a month now, since my sister died unexpectedly. Since then I’ve been feeling this way.
Do these low feelings seem mostly connected to your sister’s death?
Yes, mostly. It really started after my sister died unexpectedly, about a month ago, and I haven’t felt like myself since then.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes… I have. I still make myself go to things, like my book club or the dance night, but I don’t really enjoy them the way I used to. I’m there, but it feels like I’m sort of behind a pane of glass. Even my garden, or cooking for the neighbors… those things used to give me a little lift, and lately they just don’t.
Have you been feeling worthless, or blaming yourself in a way that feels excessive?

Yes. I keep replaying those last weeks with my sister and thinking I should have called more, or listened better, or done something more useful. Part of me knows I probably couldn’t have changed what happened, but I still blame myself for not doing more.
Have you been feeling hopeless?
I’m not sure I’d call it hopeless. I do have moments where I feel like things are very heavy, but I don’t know that I’ve really thought of it that way.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?
Yes. I don’t sleep very solidly. I sort of doze off in pieces, and then I’m awake before dawn with my mind already going. Most mornings I can’t really get settled again after that.
Since your sister died, have there still been moments when something could genuinely make you feel a little better, even briefly?

Sometimes, maybe a little, but not like before. I still make myself go to things, like book club or the dance night, but I mostly feel like I’m just sitting there, kind of separated from everyone. Even things I used to enjoy, like my garden or cooking something for the neighbors, don’t really give me that lift anymore.
When something good happens, are you able to feel even a brief lift in your mood?

Not really, no. I still make myself go to book club or the dance night, but I feel kind of behind a pane of glass. And things like my garden, or cooking something for the neighbors, they just don’t give me that little lift they used to.
Lately, have you been moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual?
I don’t think so. I mean, I feel slower inside sometimes, but I haven’t noticed myself moving or talking noticeably slower. No one’s mentioned it to me either.
Before your sister died, have you ever had another period like this where you felt depressed for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I had anything quite like this before, at least not that lasted that long, but I’d have to think about it.
Since your sister died, have you noticed your appetite has changed?
Yes, it has. Food just doesn’t really appeal to me much anymore. I’ll make a little toast or some soup, and then by the evening I realize I’ve barely eaten. I’m not trying to lose weight or anything.
Have you had thoughts of killing yourself?
I’ve had thoughts like… it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. That’s actually what scared me enough to ask for help. But I don’t have a plan to hurt myself.
Lately, have you been feeling worthless?

Yes… I have. I keep thinking back over those last weeks with my sister and telling myself I should’ve called more, or listened better, or done something more useful. Part of me knows I probably couldn’t have changed what happened, but I still feel like I failed her somehow.
Has this been making it hard for you to manage your usual day-to-day responsibilities?

Yes, it has. I’ve had to ask another volunteer to take over parts of the Juneteenth budgeting workshop because I just can’t keep up with the preparation like I normally would. And I’ve been saying no to neighbors and friends more than usual… I just don’t have it in me lately.
Since your sister died, have you found yourself intensely longing or yearning for her?
I’m not sure I’d call it intense longing. I miss her, of course, but it’s more that I think about her and what happened. I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’m yearning for her all the time.
Would you say these symptoms have significantly interfered with your daily functioning?

Yes, it has. I’m still managing some things, but not like I usually do. I had to ask another volunteer to cover parts of the Juneteenth budgeting workshop because I just couldn’t keep up with the preparation, and I’ve been turning down neighbors and friends more than I normally would.
Since your sister died, have you been feeling down most of the day nearly every day?
I don’t know if I’d say most of the day nearly every day. I’ve been feeling low, yes, but I’m not really sure how to measure it that way.
In the past month, have you felt depressed nearly every day?
I’m not really sure. I’ve had a lot of low days this past month, but I don’t know if it’s been nearly every day.

final_diagnosis.reason: Symptoms began within a month of the unexpected death of the patient's sister and are described as mostly connected to that identifiable psychosocial stressor, with depressed mood, anhedonia, guilt, insomnia, reduced appetite, passive death wishes, and functional impairment. Major depressive disorder was considered because several depressive symptoms are present for over 2 weeks, but the episode appears stressor-linked, prior episodes are not established, and the interview did not clearly confirm pervasive depressed mood nearly every day; severe MDE without psychosis is not supported because psychomotor change, clear hopelessness, and active suicidal intent/plan were not confirmed.
